Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• Diffuse myalgia and fatigue beginning ~2 weeks after return from U.S. holiday.  
• Single annular calf rash mid-to-late February that faded over 1-2 weeks; possible erythema migrans.  
• No ongoing fever, respiratory, GI, GU, or neurologic signs.  
• History of outdoor walking in shorts—possible tick exposure.

Working diagnosis  
• Suspected early Lyme disease with systemic manifestations (fatigue, arthralgia) pending serology.

Supporting differentials (consistent with transcript and DDx)  
1. Lyme disease – High likelihood: rash resembling erythema migrans after potential tick exposure; timeline fits; clinician ordering Lyme serology.  
2. Post-viral fatigue/EBV/CMV – Medium likelihood: sore throat and low-grade fever initially, persistent fatigue; single rash less typical.  
3. Hypothyroidism – Medium likelihood: fatigue and myalgia common; will screen via TSH in planned labs.

Plan  
• Order blood tests: CBC, U&E, LFTs, CRP/ESR, TSH, Lyme serology, viral serology as indicated.  
• Phone follow-up one week after labs to review results.  
• If Lyme serology positive: commence appropriate antibiotic course (e.g., doxycycline) and arrange further follow-up.  
• Provide symptom management advice and encourage graded return to normal physical activity.  
• Safety-net: advise patient to seek care if fever, neurologic symptoms, significant joint swelling, or cardiac symptoms develop.
